summary: The solver-visible StoneVault environment is a coherent crash-safe storage engine with a real Rust control plane over a C++ durable core. Roughly 3,020 lines of cpp/hpp/rs runtime code across eleven differentiated C++ modules and seven Rust modules are compiled into /app/stonevault/bin/stonevault via build.rs/Makefile/Dockerfile. Entrypoint tracing from main through protocol dispatch, FFI, and engine methods reaches WAL append/recovery, MVCC catalog, snapshot checkpointing, transaction lifecycle, codec/I/O, and cross-module integrity audits invoked by STATS. Incomplete wiring (conflict detection, scan overlay, writer lock acquire, HEALTH depth) reflects starter defects rather than unreachable padding; removing ~25% of core modules would materially collapse durability and operator behavior.

evidence.observation: Task metadata identifies a frontier database/storage workload (cpp+rust, wal/mvcc/recovery tags) with separate verifier environment, 8192MB memory, and workdir /app/stonevault—consistent with a large-system production package.
Primary operator entrypoint: opens Engine on configured data dir, emits READY, and runs a persistent REPL dispatching parsed protocol commands through session guards and FFI.

Build graph compiles all eleven storage/*.cpp modules (catalog, codec, common, engine, integrity, lock, maintenance, recovery, snapshot, transactions, wal) into libstonevault_engine.a linked by the Rust binary—no orphan compilation units.
Engine orchestrates open/recovery, mutex-guarded transactions, WAL append+sync on commit, catalog apply_commit, checkpoint via snapshot publish, and STATS/HEALTH surfaces through distinct code paths.
Append-only checksummed WAL with typed Put/Delete/Commit records, torn-tail truncation, CRC validation, pending-transaction replay, and sequence-gap detection—material persistence logic, not a stub.
restore_database chains snapshot load, WAL recover, and ordered commit replay into catalog—central restart coupling point reachable from every Engine open.
MVCC version histories with tombstones, snapshot visibility, prefix scan, conflict helper, and deep audit accounting exercised through integrity validation.
Cross-subsystem runtime audit (catalog snapshot consistency, active-transaction bounds, durable-path typing/non-aliasing, WAL size agreement) reached from Engine::stats via audit_runtime_state.
Documents wire protocol, WAL/snapshot binary layouts, transaction MVCC semantics, checkpoint lifecycle, and HEALTH/STATS operator contracts that the code implements at varying completeness.
Pinned rust:1.85-slim base, copies storage/src/docs, runs make to produce the runtime artifact at /app/stonevault.

do_not_change: solver-visible environment/ tree scope hash binding
C++/Rust module split and build.rs compilation graph
documented WAL and snapshot on-disk formats in docs/storage-format.md

role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: Approximately 3,020 lines across cpp/hpp/rs under environment/stonevault (engine 481, wal 272, catalog 224, integrity 198, snapshot 197, codec 208, transactions 186, protocol 216, ffi 319, plus maintenance/recovery/lock/common/config/session/observability/line_io/main). Adding Makefile, Dockerfile, and build.rs configuration brings the solver-visible runtime/config surface above the 3,000-line large_system_strict floor. Thin modules (lock ~21 LOC, common ~12 LOC) exist but are not dominant; the bulk is branching persistence, recovery, MVCC, and audit logic.
role_output.MAJOR_MODULES: Rust control plane: main (REPL loop), protocol (parse/execute), session (active-tx tracking), ffi (C ABI wrapper), config (data-dir resolution), line_io (bounded ASCII I/O), observability (STATS/HEALTH canonicalization). C++ durable core: engine (orchestration+FFI exports), wal (append/recover/truncate), recovery (snapshot+WAL restore), catalog (MVCC histories/scan/conflicts), snapshot (load/publish binary format), transactions (active table+overlay helper), integrity (cross-module audits), codec (CRC/hex/fsync/file I/O), maintenance (path prep/stats render), lock (writer lock fd lifecycle), common (byte-order key comparator).
role_output.PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Commit conflict detection requires wiring catalog.conflicts into engine commit while keeping WAL sequence contiguity; scan correctness needs apply_transaction_overlay on catalog scan results; checkpoint BUSY semantics must coordinate snapshot.tmp cleanup, rename+dir sync, and WAL reset; HEALTH must run integrity audits not stubbed constants; WriterLock must acquire exclusive flock on open; WAL torn-tail vs corruption classification must stay aligned with docs; fixing snapshot row CRC in load without matching publish breaks checkpoint round-trips; session-layer active-tx tracking can diverge from engine if BEGIN/COMMIT responses change shape.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Deleting wal+recovery (~286 LOC) removes crash recovery entirely. Deleting catalog+snapshot (~421 LOC) removes durable key-value state. Deleting integrity (~198 LOC) removes STATS cross-audit behavior documented as production operator surface. Removing ~750 LOC (~25%) from these subsystems would collapse the engine from a crash-safe MVCC store into a non-durable in-memory toy regardless of Rust protocol scaffolding.
